ai.title: Opaque CLI auth tokens replace raw auth codes in login URLs
ai.summary: CLI login URLs now use opaque 43-character tokens instead of exposing raw signed auth payloads. The web API generates these tokens via `randomBytes` and stores them in `verificationToken` under `cli-login:<token>`, while the onboard page resolves them using `DELETE ... RETURNING` to ensure single-use consumption. This change applies to both `freebuff/web` and `web` packages, specifically updating `route.ts`, `_db.ts`, `_helpers.ts`, and `page.tsx`, alongside `docs/authentication.md`. Opaque tokens are strictly validated against `/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{43}$/` before database lookup.

eli5.text: When you sign in to the service using the command-line tool, the web page now generates a random, non-readable code instead of exposing a signed authentication payload directly in the login URL. This opaque code is stored behind the scenes and resolved only once during onboarding, then deleted. This change applies to both the freebuff/web and web packages, affecting the CLI login flow and onboarding process. The change is in place today as part of the latest release, tightening how CLI authentication tokens are handled for improved security.

ai.title: Add CLI auth token correlation fields to logs
ai.summary: Added getCliAuthCodeHashPrefix to compute SHA-256 hash prefixes for opaque CLI auth tokens. Updated auth code issuance and resolution logs to include token hash prefixes, lengths, and request origin details for better traceability. Changes apply to web/src/app/api/auth/cli/code/route.ts, web/src/app/onboard/_helpers.ts, and web/src/app/onboard/page.tsx. Uses node:crypto createHash for 12-char hex digest prefix.

eli5.text: When you sign in with the CLI tool, the system now writes extra tracking details into its logs including a short, scrambled version of the login token (made by running it through a secure one-way fingerprint process), how long the token is, and where the request came from. This doesn't change how you log in or what you see, but if someone is troubleshooting a signup issue they will find more precise clues in the logs without exposing the real token. The change is live today across both the Freebuff sign-in flow and the Codebuff sign-in flow.

ai.title: SDK path-utils tolerates absolute file tool paths
ai.summary: Added sdk/src/tools/path-utils.ts exporting resolveFilePathWithinProject and getProjectPathLookupKeys. File tools (change-file, read-files, run.ts) now use these helpers instead of inline path.normalize/isAbsolute checks, allowing absolute paths that resolve within the project root while still blocking traversal outside it. Covers SDK core and tools; no CLI/Web surface changes.

eli5.text: The SDK's file-handling tools can now accept either relative or absolute file paths as long as the file lives inside your project folder, instead of rejecting any path that doesn't start from the project root. Absolute paths that point outside your project still get blocked, preserving the existing safety check. Developers using the SDK tools internally will notice they can pass paths like `/home/user/project/src/code.ts` or `src/code.ts` interchangeably without errors. The change is already active in the current SDK version.

ai.title: Hide code searcher result payload
ai.summary: Code searcher agent now sets `message: ''` in `set_output` to prevent raw structured payload leakage in CLI. `CodeSearchComponent` parses `Found N matches` header for total results, falling back to line counting with `Line \d+:` regex support. Covers `agents/file-explorer/code-searcher.ts` and `cli/src/components/tools/code-search.tsx`. `docs/testing.md` adds tmux workflow examples for verifying UI captures.

eli5.text: When you ask the tool to search through your code, it now hides the raw, jumbled technical details of what it found and only shows you a clean summary line like "Found 7 matches" instead of dumping the full internal results data into your terminal. Behind the scenes, the search agent now sends an empty message field when reporting results, and the display component reads the match-count header to figure out how many hits there were. The documentation also adds step-by-step tmux commands so testers can capture and replay a terminal session to verify the cleaner output.

ai.title: Freebuff 1.0.674 ships OpenCode Zen routing and opaque CLI auth tokens
ai.summary: Freebuff 1.0.674 consolidates a day of CLI auth hardening and provider updates. CLI login now uses opaque 43-char base64url tokens validated by `/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{43}$/`, stored in `verificationToken` under `cli-login:<token>` and consumed once by the onboard page via `DELETE ... RETURNING`. OpenCode Zen routing now activates for any `opencode/` prefix instead of an allowlist, with `isOpenCodeZenModel` gaining a `model is string` type guard and the previous 400 `opencode_zen_disabled` gate removed. Code searcher agent sets `message: ''` to suppress payload leakage, and SDK file tools now accept absolute paths resolving within the project root via `resolveFilePathWithinProject`.
ai.evidence: Diff hunk in `cli/release/package.json` changes `version` from `1.0.673` to `1.0.674`, a single-line release bump in the release packaging manifest. Modified file listed as `cli/release/package.json`.

eli5.text: This release upgrades your Freebuff experience by adding smarter AI model routing, more secure login, and better search results in the terminal. Now, any model name starting with 'opencode/' (like opencode/minimax-m2.7 and opencode/kimi-k2.6) gets automatically routed through OpenCode Zen, so you can use those models without extra setup, while legacy hyphen-style login codes are still accepted for older apps. Your CLI login is now safer: instead of exposing a raw signed payload in login URLs, Freebuff hands out an opaque 43-character token stored in the database, which is deleted after single use so login links can't be replayed or tampered with. The built-in code searcher now hides raw structured output from your terminal and cleanly reports how many matches it found, so your screen stays readable. Upgrading means smoother model access, stronger login security, and a cleaner, safer command-line search experience every day.

ai.title: Freebuff 0.0.85 release bumps version from 0.0.84
ai.summary: Freebuff 0.0.85 ships OpenCode Zen routing for any model string prefixed with `opencode/`, replacing the earlier hardcoded allowlist. CLI login flow now issues random 32-byte base64url opaque tokens instead of exposing raw signed auth payloads in login URLs. SDK file tools now tolerate absolute file tool paths that resolve within the project root. Code searcher agent now blanks its `set_output` message to prevent structured payload leakage in CLI output.
ai.evidence: The commit bumps the version field in freebuff/cli/release/package.json from "0.0.84" to "0.0.85".

eli5.text: Freebuff 0.0.85 delivers a new way to connect with certain AI model families through OpenCode Zen routing, along with stronger security and privacy improvements in login, code search, and file handling. The new OpenCode Zen support activates automatically for any model name that starts with "opencode/", so users can access new models like minimax-m2.8 and kimi-k2.6 once an API key is added, and the login system now uses secret, one-time tokens in URLs instead of exposing raw signed authentication data, which keeps your credentials safer. Code searching no longer leaks internal structured data into the terminal and instead shows a clean summary of how many matches were found, and file-based tools now accept absolute file paths as long as they stay within your project folder. Additionally, legacy login codes from older CLI clients still work through an automatic compatibility fallback, while new logging adds traceability and debuggability of login attempts. Upgrading means you get access to new model integrations, more secure and private login flows, cleaner search results, and more reliable file-path handling when using the Freebuff tools.
